summary: First full iteration: backend pytest suite (10 tests, 100% pass) covering GET /api/, POST /api/contact happy path + persistence, 422 validation matrix, GET /api/contact ordering and no _id leakage. Frontend Playwright testing on desktop (1920x1080) and mobile (390x844): logo/hero/platforms, EL<->EN language switching (nav, hero, client tags, English client name mapping), desktop nav scroll, stats counters (100M+, 28+, 1,200+, 4), all 28 client names in the two marquee rows (56 cards, 28 unique ids, no text truncation), contact form submit with success toast + persistence verified via GET /api/contact, no console errors, no horizontal overflow. One real bug found: mobile menu links close the menu but never scroll to the section.

minor.issue: Publicly readable with no auth - leaks all submitter names/emails/messages (PII). Should be protected or removed from the public API.
deliver_email() is awaited inline with a 20s timeout, so a slow formsubmit.co response blocks the request and the user's form submit; consider background task with Mongo-first write.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking mobile-nav-services/results/clients/contact closes the menu but the page does NOT scroll (scrollY stays 0 across all frames and after 4s). Desktop nav-* buttons work fine and a raw document.getElementById('clients').scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}) works, so the failure is in go() - the setOpen(false) re-render / AnimatePresence exit animation cancels the smooth scroll. Suggested fix: defer the scroll (e.g. requestAnimationFrame/setTimeout after closing) or scroll before closing the menu.

issues: Cards at the row edges are half-visible behind the edge-fade mask (expected for a marquee, noted only for awareness).

action_items: Fix mobile menu navigation: mobile-nav-* buttons must scroll to their sections (defer scrollIntoView until after the menu close re-render)
Consider protecting GET /api/contact (currently public PII listing)
Optional: move formsubmit.co email delivery off the request path
critical_code_review_comments: Navbar.go(): calling setOpen(false) and scrollIntoView in the same tick breaks smooth scroll for the mobile menu; scroll must be scheduled after the exit animation starts.
GET /api/contact has no auth/rate limiting and returns up to 500 raw submissions including emails.
server.py uses deprecated @app.on_event('shutdown'); prefer FastAPI lifespan handlers.
seed_data_creation: Created 4 TEST_* contact docs during testing (2 via API, 2 via the UI form); all were deleted from the contacts collection afterwards (collection is now empty).
test_credentials: N/A - app has no auth (/app/memory/test_credentials.md not needed)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (pytest, uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env; pytest.ini runs with xdist). Everything passes. Only open defect is mobile-menu navigation not scrolling; retest at 390x844 by opening data-testid='mobile-menu-toggle' then clicking mobile-nav-clients and asserting window.scrollY > 0. All 28 client names, i18n, stats counters, contact form + persistence already verified.
rca_of_the_issue: Navbar go(id) executes setOpen(false) followed immediately by element.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}). On mobile the state change unmounts the menu via AnimatePresence, and the resulting re-render/layout animation aborts the browser's programmatic smooth-scroll animation before it advances, so scrollY never changes. Reproduced deterministically 3/3 times on 390x844; desktop path (no state change) scrolls correctly.
